images.title: Same quotient, new numbers
images.purpose: Recap the topic's method as an equivalent fraction: multiply the top and bottom by the same 100 so the divisor becomes a counting number.
images.composition: One large fraction chain in the centre, reading left to right, with two small curved arrows above and below; plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Centre, left to right: the fraction 7.2 over 0.08, an equals sign =, the fraction 720 over 8, an equals sign =, the number 90; the two fraction bars are plain dark lines.
A teal #0072B2 curved arrow above, from 7.2 to 720, labelled × 100.
An amber #E69F00 curved arrow below, from 0.08 to 8, labelled × 100.
The divisor 8 is circled in reddish purple #CC79A7 and the answer 90 is green #009E73.
rejection: any value other than 720 over 8 or the answer 90
the two arrows carrying different multipliers
the fraction drawn upside down (0.08 on top)
images.takeaway: Multiplying the top and bottom by the same number keeps the quotient, so 7.2 ÷ 0.08 = 720 ÷ 8 = 90.
images.description: The fraction 7.2 over 0.08 becomes 720 over 8 by multiplying top and bottom by 100, equal to 90.
images.context: Shown beside the practice task on dividing by a decimal.

image_decisions.why: A compact fraction view recaps the method with fresh numbers that give nothing away.
